figures.caption: Figure 1: An illustration of the NMA setting of Table 2. The treatment nodes are connected by edges coloured by study k = 1, k = 2, and k = 3. The absence of an edge between (d) and (e) indicates that no study directly comparing these treatments is available.

Figure 8: Network meta-analysis under heterogeneous populations and no center effect (τpop = 1, σu = σv = 0; see Table 4), over 200 Monte-Carlo replications. Each treatment is contrasted against the anchor a = 0 on the RD, log risk-ratio and log odds-ratio scales; points are Monte-Carlo means and bars the 2.5–97.5% range, with the red dashed line the causal truth Φ(ψ∗a, ψ∗0) on the uniform mixture of the study populations.

Figure 7: Network meta-analysis under homogeneous populations and no center effect (τpop = 0, σu = σv = 0; see Table 4), over 200 Monte-Carlo replications. Each treatment is contrasted against the anchor a = 0 on the RD, log risk-ratio and log odds-ratio scales; points are Monte-Carlo means and bars the 2.5–97.5% range of the estimates, with the red dashed line the causal truth. CL-FE and CL-RE are fitted with netmeta; the causal estimator uses the between-study delta-method variance of Section 4.2.

Figure 10: Re-analysis of the bleeding-reduction network of Gurusamy et al. (2011), same layout as Figure 9. Here the network is sparse: CL-FE and CL-RE coincide (heterogeneity estimated at zero) and their intervals are very wide, while the causal intervals are markedly tighter and occasionally significant where CL is not.

Figure 9: Re-analysis of the atrial-fibrillation network of Dogliotti et al. (2014): each antithrombotic strategy is contrasted against control on the RD, log risk-ratio and log odds-ratio scales, using CLFE, CL-RE (netmeta) and the causal arm-level estimator of Section 4.2. Points are estimates and bars 95% confidence intervals. The three methods agree on direction; the causal intervals are somewhat wider on this dense network.

Figure 6: Monte-Carlo distributions (B = 200 replications) of the FE, RE and causal estimators of the contrast between A = 1 and A = 0 in the fully heterogeneous pairwise setting (τpop = 1, σu = σv = 0.5, K = 10, n = 4000, uniform weights). Left: risk difference; middle: log risk-ratio; right: log odds-ratio. The red dashed line is the causal estimand θ(µ⋆, P ⋆) of Section 3.5, averaged over replications.
Table 3: Estimators by population and center effect assumptions.
